open_points.subject: function purity and admission
open_points.text: “A flow is a small proven graph of two kinds of node: a pure function an agent wrote” and “No effectful, stateful or network-capable function” conflict with “code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
open_points.question: Is purity a required fact of every admitted implementation, or does “pure function” now mean only that the kernel blocks the named capabilities and otherwise admits code solely from observed trial outputs?
options: Every admitted function must actually be independent of time and chance, even when the dependency uses an unblocked route.
An implementation using an unblocked time or chance source may be admitted if its observed trial outputs pass; purity is only the enforced capability boundary.
open_points.default_guess: Treat purity as the enforced capability boundary and admit an undetected implementation when its trial executions pass.

witness.initial: A contract version has a nonempty trial corpus whose case requires only valid output, without expected_outputs.
events: An authoring agent submits an implementation that obtains chance through a route other than the standard-library entry points that raise.
The kernel runs admission and the observed output satisfies the contract and case.
The owner or agent later runs a flow containing that function.
outcomes: The implementation is refused because an admitted function must factually be pure and independent of chance.
The implementation is admitted and activated because the alternate chance dependency is not detected and its observed outputs pass; later runs may return different valid outputs.
witness.observer: The submitting agent and later run readers see whether the implementation was admitted and whether the flow can run.

open_points.subject: AdmissionVerdict identity under nondeterministic executions
open_points.text: “Admission is a deterministic verdict over the whole active corpus”; “Substitution: a verdict for the same implementation and corpus is the same verdict”; and “every active case of the corpus is run again for the implementation at admission time” conflict once “code written to get time or chance some other way is not detected and is judged by its outputs like any other.”
open_points.question: When the same implementation is submitted again against the unchanged corpus and its newly run trial executions produce a different result, is the existing AdmissionVerdict reused, or is a distinct verdict created—and if distinct, what gives it identity and which verdict controls activation or rollback eligibility?
options: Reuse the one existing verdict for the implementation and corpus, without allowing later observations to change it.
Rerun admission and create a distinct verdict for each admission observation, despite the stated value identity.
Rerun admission and replace or mutate the verdict associated with that implementation and corpus.
open_points.default_guess: Rerun on every submission and treat the resulting verdict as distinct evidence identified by that admission's TrialExecutions; use the new verdict for that submission's activation decision.

witness.initial: One contract version has one authored case expecting output false; an implementation for it uses an undetected alternate source of chance.
events: The agent submits the implementation; its admission execution returns false, so it is admitted and activated.
The agent submits equal code for the same contract version again; this returns the existing implementation identity.
Admission runs the unchanged case again, and this execution returns true.
outcomes: Because implementation and corpus are unchanged and their AdmissionVerdict is one value, the existing admitted verdict is returned or remains authoritative.
Because every submission reruns every case and verdict follows those executions, the second submission produces a refused verdict for the same implementation and corpus.
witness.observer: The submitting agent sees a different admission result, and activation or later rollback checks may see different eligibility.
